uncited: Output is a single unsigned integer (Morton code).
It iterates over each bit position $i$ from 0 to $B-1$ (where $B$ is the number of bits per coordinate, e.g., 21 for 64-bit codes in 3D).
Extract the $i$-th bit of each coordinate $x_k$: $b_k = (x_k \gg i) \& 1$.
Place $b_k$ into the $k \cdot N + i$-th position of the result, where $N$ is the number of dimensions.
The standard Z-order interleaves bits at position $i$ of each coordinate into positions $i, i+N, i+2N, \dots$ of the code.
**Spread X:** Spread the bits of $x$ into even positions.
For 3D, the shift amounts are 0, 1, 2 relative to the spread bits).*
*   **Time Complexity:** Naive encoding/decoding is $O(B)$ where $B$ is the number of bits per coordinate.
Not suitable for very large coordinate spaces without multi-word codes.
*   **When not to use:** When coordinates exceed bit limits.
